options.text: I sometimes watch movies on Fridays.

questions.context: A conversation about living in different cities.

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative sentence about a person's routine.

options.text: He don't play video games on Mondays.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "He" requires the auxiliary "doesn't".

options.text: He doesn't play video games on Mondays.
options.feedback: Correct! "Doesn't" is the correct auxiliary for third person singular.

options.text: He doesn't plays video games on Mondays.
options.feedback: Incorrect. After "doesn't", the verb must be in its base form (no 's').

options.text: He not play video games on Mondays.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Missing the auxiliary verb "do/does".

questions.explanation:
The student applies the rules for negative sentences in the third-person singular.

questions.statement: What can we analyze from their habits?
questions.context:
Comparing two students' schedules.
"Ana: Studies 5 days a week / Plays sport 1 day a week / Reads every night."
"Luis: Studies 5 days a week / Plays sport 3 days a week / Never reads."

options.text: Ana plays sport more often than Luis.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Luis plays sport 3 days, Ana only 1.

options.text: Ana reads more frequently than Luis.
options.feedback: Correct! Ana reads every night, Luis never reads.
Incorrect. They both study the same amount (5 days).
Incorrect. Their sport and reading habits are different.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes and compares frequency data to identify a correct descriptive statement.

questions.statement: Which conclusion is most valid based on Mateo's description?
questions.context:
Evaluating a description of a person.
"Mateo is very athletic. He usually runs 10 kilometers before school, he always eats vegetables, and he never drinks soda. He is the captain of the soccer team."

options.text: Mateo is the captain because he never drinks soda.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is only one part of his healthy habits, not the sole reason.

options.text: Mateo runs because he doesn't have time to sleep.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text doesn't mention his sleep habits.

options.text: Mateo's disciplined and healthy habits support his role as an athlete.
options.feedback: Correct! The combination of exercise and diet reflects his athletic nature and discipline.

options.text: Mateo always eats vegetables because he is the captain.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The relationship is likely the other way around: his habits make him a good candidate for captain.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates a set of behavioral facts to determine the most comprehensive and logical conclusion.
